guide.summary: Box supports OAuth 2.0 for third-party apps and Composio offers a managed Box app, so you can prototype without registering anything. A custom Box User app is quick to create (free developer account, redirect URI, scopes). The main friction: in enterprises that keep unpublished apps inactive by default, a Box Admin must enable your Client ID. No review timeline is documented.

composio.note: Composio lists Box under Composio-managed OAuth. Switch to a custom auth config for your own consent-screen branding, custom scopes or dedicated quota.

need_own_app.answer: Not to start. Use Composio's managed Box app for prototypes and internal tools. Create your own Box User (OAuth 2.0) app for production branding, custom scopes or dedicated rate-limit quota.
reasons: Users see your app name instead of 'Composio' on the consent screen
Default scopes may not match what you need
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users; your own app gets dedicated quota
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers; your own app may allow shorter
Enterprise customers may require your branding end to end

scenarios.label: Prototype on Composio managed app
scenarios.when_this_applies: Building or testing, or internal use, where 'Composio' on the consent screen is acceptable.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured; no provider app to register (c1, c2)

scenarios.approval: None from Box for you. The user's enterprise admin policy may still apply (see unknown in open questions).

scenarios.label: Own app, free developer account
scenarios.when_this_applies: Own-brand custom auth config, used with a free developer (Individual) account.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count: create User app, set redirect URI and scopes, create Composio auth config (c4, c5, c6)

waiting.basis: Apps from free developer accounts are authorized automatically.

scenarios.approval: Automatic authorization for free developer accounts.

scenarios.label: Own app, used inside enterprise Box accounts
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your users or customers are in Box enterprise accounts.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count: s2 steps plus requesting admin approval (c8, c9)

waiting.basis: Depends on the customer's Box Admin; no timeline documented.

scenarios.approval: Only if the enterprise keeps unpublished apps inactive by default: a Box Admin or Co-Admin enables the app by Client ID. Re-authorization is needed after scope changes.

scenarios.label: Box Integrations marketplace listing
scenarios.when_this_applies: You want public listing for discovery. Optional.

hands_on.basis: estimate: submission form, description, screenshots, icon (c12)

waiting.basis: Docs say the Box Partner team reviews 'as soon as possible'; no duration given.

prerequisites.title: Composio account and API key
prerequisites.detail: Needed to create the auth config via dashboard or API.

prerequisites.title: Box developer account
prerequisites.detail: A free developer account gives Developer Console access to create OAuth 2.0 apps. An enterprise account works if you have Developer Console access.

prerequisites.title: Box Admin contact (enterprise scenarios)
prerequisites.detail: You need an admin who can authorize your Client ID. Check the Admin Contact at the bottom of Box Account Settings.

prerequisites.title: Listing assets (marketplace only)
prerequisites.detail: Categories, short and long descriptions, Add button URL, screenshots and app icon.

steps.title: Prototype with the Composio managed Box app
steps.detail: Create a Composio session or auth config using the managed `box` toolkit and run a test connection. No Box registration needed.
steps.done_when: A Box connection shows active in Composio.

steps.title: Create a Box User app
steps.detail: In the Developer Console choose New App, then User, then Create. The type cannot be changed to Server later.
inputs: Box developer or enterprise account login
steps.done_when: The app appears under My Platform Apps.

steps.title: Copy the callback URI from the Composio dashboard
steps.detail: Get the redirect URI from your Composio dashboard for the Box auth config; do not hard-code it. Box needs an exact match, so use the exact string. If you want the browser to stay on your domain, use a redirect proxy that 302-redirects to Composio.
steps.done_when: You have the exact callback URI string.

steps.title: Register the redirect URI and scopes in Box
steps.detail: On the Configuration tab add the redirect URI under OAuth 2.0 Redirect URI (HTTPS, no duplicates) and select the scopes your tools need. The agent can draft the scope list from the Composio tools you use.
steps.done_when: Saved on the Configuration tab with the exact URI.

steps.title: Create the Composio custom auth config
steps.detail: Create the Box auth config with your Client ID and Client Secret from the Configuration tab (OAuth 2.0 Credentials), via the Composio API or dashboard.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists and a test connection completes the Box consent screen.

steps.title: If needed, submit the app for admin enablement
steps.detail: Only where unpublished apps are inactive by default: submit on the Enablement tab (emails the Primary Admin), or give the Client ID to your Box Admin to add under Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps.
steps.done_when: Admin approves; you receive an email decision.

steps.title: Wait for the admin, if enablement was needed
steps.detail: Blocked on the customer's Box Admin or Co-Admin.
steps.done_when: The app is authorized or enabled.

steps.title: Re-authorize after scope changes
steps.detail: If you change scopes or access level, re-authorize (auto for free developer accounts, admin action for enterprise).
steps.done_when: The Configuration tab shows no pending changes.

steps.title: Prepare the marketplace listing text
steps.detail: Draft categories, short and long descriptions and support information; list the required screenshots and icon.
steps.done_when: The form content is ready to paste.

steps.title: Submit for Approval on the Publishing tab
steps.detail: Confirm the checklist, fill in the form and click Submit for Approval. Questions go to integrate@box.com.

steps.title: Wait for Box Partner team review

traps.title: Exact redirect URI match
traps.detail: Box checks the redirect_uri exactly. A mismatch with the Composio callback (or your proxy) breaks the flow.

traps.title: Multiple redirect URIs need the parameter
traps.detail: If several URIs are configured and redirect_uri is not sent, users see redirect_uri_missing.

traps.title: App type is permanent
traps.detail: A User (OAuth) app cannot be converted to Server, or the reverse.

traps.title: Custom apps count toward the enterprise API allocation
traps.detail: Calls from custom apps count toward the customer's monthly API allocation, so heavy agent use can hit licensing-based limits.

traps.title: Per-user rate limits
traps.detail: About 1000 API calls per minute per user; search is limited to 6 per second and 60 per minute per user.

traps.title: Managed app shared quota and polling
traps.detail: The managed app shares quota across Composio users, and triggers poll no faster than every 15 minutes.

blockers.symptom: User from an enterprise cannot connect; app is not authorized or enabled
blockers.what_it_means: The enterprise's Box Admin must authorize or enable your Client ID.
blockers.what_to_do: Submit from the Enablement tab or send the Client ID to the admin to add under Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the request email to the admin including the Client ID and scopes.

blockers.what_it_means: The redirect URI is not sent or does not exactly match a configured URI.
blockers.what_to_do: Copy the callback URI from the Composio dashboard into Box exactly.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare the configured URI string against the one the connect link uses.

blockers.what_to_do: Wait for the retry-after seconds and back off exponentially.

blockers.what_it_means: The app needs re-authorization after scope changes.

open_questions: Review duration for Box Integrations listing: not documented. Ask integrate@box.com or check the Box community forum.
Whether consent shows warnings for unapproved apps, and any test-user or connection caps for unapproved OAuth apps: not found. Test with a second account.
Monthly API allocation figures and Platform API pricing: on https://www.box.com/pricing, not read.
Whether Box verifies domain ownership of redirect URIs: not found in the docs read; the callback must still match exactly.
Whether enterprise admin policies block the Composio managed app Client ID for some customers: not documented; ask the customer admin.
Whether Box requires a security assessment or business verification: not found in the docs read.

claims.text: Composio lists Box as having Composio-managed OAuth available.
claims.quote: **Composio-managed OAuth available?** Yes
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: With a managed app, you do not need to register an OAuth app or supply client ID and secret.
claims.quote: You do not need to register an OAuth app or supply its client ID and client secret.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Managed apps are suited to building and iterating, where consent-screen branding does not matter yet.
claims.quote: **Branding on consent screens doesn't matter yet.**
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: A free developer account gives access to the Developer Console, where you can create and configure OAuth 2.0 apps.
claims.quote: A free developer account gives you access to the Developer Console, where you can create and configure OAuth 2.0 applications.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: To create an OAuth 2.0 app, select New App and choose User as the app type.
claims.quote: 3. Select **User** as the app type.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Box checks that redirect_uri exactly matches a configured redirect URI.
claims.quote: This will be an exact match check, meaning the URIs must be exactly the same.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: For free developer accounts, app authorization happens automatically when the app is created.
claims.quote: For free developer accounts, authorization happens automatically when the app is created.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: A Box Admin or Co-Admin needs an application's Client ID to authorize or enable it in the Admin Console.
claims.quote:
A Box Admin or Co-Admin needs an application's Client ID to authorize or
enable it in the Admin Console.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Unpublished OAuth 2.0 apps may require enablement by a Box Admin or Co-Admin if inactive by default.
claims.quote:
Unpublished applications using OAuth 2.0 authentication may
require enablement by a Box Admin or Co-Admin if they are inactive by default.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Submitting from the Enablement tab emails the enterprise's Primary Admin to approve the app.
claims.quote:
Submitting the application for approval sends an email to your
enterprise's Primary Admin to approve the application.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: When an app's scopes or access level change, it must be re-authorized.
claims.quote: When an application's scopes or access level change, the application must be re-authorized for the changes to take effect.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: To list in Box Integrations, the app must be production-ready and use OAuth 2.0, then be submitted via the Publishing tab.
claims.quote: The platform app leverages OAuth 2.0 authentication, as Integrations do not support any other authentication methods.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: After submission, the Box Partner team reviews the request as soon as possible, with no stated duration.
claims.quote: the Box Partner team will be notified and review your request as soon as possible.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: If an admin contact is set, it appears at the bottom of Box Account Settings.
claims.quote: If an admin contact is set, their contact information displays under **Admin Contact**.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Once created, an OAuth 2.0 app cannot be changed to Server Authentication or the reverse.
claims.quote:
Once you create an OAuth 2.0 app, you cannot change it to Server
  Authentication (or the other way around).
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Composio documents proxying the OAuth redirect through your own domain, with a 302 redirect to Composio.
claims.quote: If you need to hide Composio's domain, you can proxy the redirect through your own domain instead.
claims.label: unknown
claims.note: The claim states 302, which the quote does not contain.

claims.text: The proxy endpoint must return a 302 redirect, not follow it server-side.
claims.quote: Your endpoint must return a **302 redirect**.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Redirect URIs must be HTTPS (HTTP only for localhost or loopback) and duplicates cannot be saved.
claims.quote:
We do not
permit duplicate URIs to be saved.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Composio custom auth configs let you provide your own OAuth app credentials for a toolkit.
claims.quote: You provide your own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tell Composio to use them for a toolkit.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: With multiple redirect URIs configured, omitting redirect_uri gives a redirect_uri_missing error.
claims.quote:
If the parameter is not specified, the user will see a `redirect_uri_missing`
  error and will not be redirected back to the app after granting application
  access.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Calls from custom applications count toward the enterprise's monthly API allocation.
claims.quote:
Calls from custom applications, scripts, and integrations count toward your
enterprise's monthly allocation, including authentication requests.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: General API calls are limited to 1000 requests per minute per user.
claims.quote: 1000 API requests per minute, per user
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users.
claims.quote: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers.
claims.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Rate-limited requests return HTTP 429 with a retry-after header.
claims.quote:
The `retry-after` header provides guidance on the number of seconds to wait
  before the next API call can be retried.
claims.label: provider_docs

meta.review_note: Summary and the enterprise setup edited by hand on 20 Oct 2026: they said an admin must always authorize the app, while the guide's own evidence says OAuth 2.0 apps need enablement only where unpublished apps are inactive by default.
